newsitem.title: UK: Panamax sector nervous in freight market.
newsitem.headline: Panamax sector nervous in freight market.

text.p: There is a war of nerves taking place in the freight market, or at least in the Panamax section which comprises 70 percent of the Baltic Freight Index (BFI).

Most owners' brokers claim that despite some examples of softer rates in the atlantic the underlying tone remains good and also that so far the widely forecast decline in the Pacific has yet to be proved.

But many observers would agree that the panamax market is nervous, eecially following the first decline recorded by the BFI since September 25, down 1 point to 1521. They believe that the immediate direction of the market is difficult to read.
Meanwhile Caper rates are still holding up, but the performance of handy-sizes is mixed.

GRAIN - A number of US Gulf/Japan fixtures have been reported today, all at lower levels. Dreyfus were linked with Istria for 52,000 heavy grain for end Nov at $25.25 no combiantion and an unnamed vessel for early Dec at a dollar less, but some brokers thought that the second fixture may have been concluded a little while ago.
Fortune was reported booked for Nov/Dec dates by unnamed charterers at $25.00 no combination.
The 1975-built Agrari was believed fixed by Dreyfus for about 55,000 grains USGulf/China for Nov 14/18 at lumpsum equivalent of $22.50 basis heavy grain or $25.00 basis lights, down from last fixed.

Timecharter levels appeared steadier than voyage rates. Farenco booked the CMT-relet Anangel Omonia 73,500 dwt delivery Antwerp Nov 21 trip via USGulf to the far East at close to $15,350 daily and Glencore took the prompt 1978-built Timios Stavros 64,370 dwt from USGulf to China at a solid $13,250 daily plus $275,000 bonus.

Oinoussian Sky 64,456 dwt was reported fixed on the same route on subjects by Pan Ocean with Nov/Dec delivery at $14,500 daily plus $300,000 bonus. A sister vessel, Oinoussian Strength, was rumoured covered by Egyptian charterers delivery Fos Nov 20 for a transatlantic round but full details were lacking, as also about Alpheos 63,640 dwt believed fixed delivery USGulf for 3-5 months timecharter.
Cargill booked a vessel for USGulf/Continent grain but of less than Panamax size.

No new Panamax grain orders were quoted in the market this morning. Brokers said the South American area was tighter for tonnage, especially for modern types, but the 1988-built Decurion 64,211 dwt open spot Recalada was said to be indicating for business out of the USGulf.

MINERALS - Rumours that Gateway Bulker 151,439 dwt fixed British Steel from Australia were discounted although it was understood that these charterers were trading New Harvest 208,739 dwt today for business to UK.
Panamax coal rates appeared to be holding up in the east with K line booking Bunga Saga Tiga 73,496 dwt from Japan Nov 20/23 for an Australian coal round at $13,450 daily.

Navix were rumoured to have taken Rubin Rosebay 69,100 dwt for an Australian round at about $13,300 daily. Reports circulated that ASA fixed a Panamax, possibly Nordscout 63,900 dwt or Nordmoritz 72,500 dwt, for an Australian round at $12,750 daily.
Nyk were linked with similar business and Showa were said to have booked a Panamax for ironore from India to Japan, both on private terms.

The middle east was still firm - the 1975-built Hunter 72,059 dwt, having failed yesterday with Glencore on subjects for a trip via South Africa with coal to China at $10,250 daily, fixed instead to Noble for a trip via India or S.Africa to China at $50 less.

HANDIES - MSL chartered Marilis t 28,097 dwt delivery Lisbon trip via Continent to the far East on private terms and Halla booked a 38,000 dwt vessel on subjects from Recife to Iran at $8,000 daily plus $200,000 bonus.

Olympic Melody 29,640 dwt, having fixed Van Ommeren delivery spot Hamburg for 2-4 months redelivery Atlantic at $7,950 daily, was immediately relet to Combac delivery Antwerp trip USGulf at $7,500 daily.
